## Purpose

This document is a working table of contents (down to the third level) for the
five slide decks used in the 2025 MathCamp session
(`Resources/Slide Decks 2025/`). It's meant to give a quick overview of what
was covered last year, to inform how we scope and sequence the new
Quarto-book-based, interactive version of the material for 2026.

## Lecture 1 — Notation, Functions, and Limits {#sec-l1}

*`SlideDeck1_081825.pdf`, Aug 18, 2025*

### Introduction & Logistics
- Introductions
- Math camp goals, logistics, and schedule
- What are quantitative methods? Quantitative vs. qualitative methods

### Variables & Measures
- Variables and constants
- Sets and sample spaces
- Unions, intersections, subsets (set notation)
- Levels of measurement, and why it matters

### Rules of Algebra
- Basic properties of arithmetic
- Order of operations
- Inequalities
- Exponents, logarithms, and roots

### Functions
- Functions and their characteristics
- Function composition
- Graph examples: linear, quadratic, exponential functions
- Functions and theorizing; Anscombe's quartet

### Solving Equations
- Special products and factoring
- Quadratics and special products
- Quadratic formula, checking work graphically

### Series, Sequences, and Limits
- Sequences and series
- Limits (including piecewise function examples)

---

## Lecture 2 — Probability {#sec-l2}

*`SlideDeck2_081925.pdf`, Aug 19, 2025*

### Introduction
- Agenda
- Frequentist vs. Bayesian framing

### Bayesian Probability
- Definitions and notation
- Relationships between events
- Bayes' theorem (notation, derivation, examples)
- The Monty Hall problem
- Odds and odds ratios

### Frequentist Statistics
- Frequentist methods and uncertainty
- Confidence interval demonstration in R

### Combinations and Permutations
- Review of factorials
- Combinations (why the formulas work, worked examples)
- Calculating probabilities; the birthday problem

### Distributions
- Random variables: discrete vs. continuous
- Sample distributions and contingency tables
- Probability distributions: PMF, PDF, CDF
- Normal/Gaussian distribution and other distribution types

---

## Lecture 3 — Calculus I: Differentiation & Optimization {#sec-l3}

*`SlideDeck3_082025.pdf`, Aug 20, 2025*

### Differentiation
- Types of change and derivatives
- Discrete change (secant lines) vs. instantaneous change (tangent lines)
- Rules of differentiation: power, product, quotient, and chain rules
- Worked examples and practice

### Optimization
- What is optimization?
- Extreme value theorem
- Derivatives and the shape of a function
- Inflection points vs. extrema
- Worked optimization example

---

## Lecture 4 — Calculus II: Integration & Multivariate Calculus {#sec-l4}

*`SlideDeck4_082125.pdf`, Aug 21, 2025*

### Integration
- Area under the curve
- Integrals and the fundamental theorem of calculus
- Reversing the rules of differentiation ("don't forget the C!")
- Rules of integration, worked examples
- Integration by substitution

### Multivariate Calculus
- Partial derivatives
- Gradients and mixed partial derivatives
- The Hessian matrix
- Application: deriving Ordinary Least Squares (OLS)

---

## Lecture 5 — Linear Algebra {#sec-l5}

*`SlideDeck5_082225.pdf`, Aug 22, 2025*

### Equations & Systems of Equations
- Equations and unknowns
- Solving by substitution and elimination
- More complex systems of equations

### Vectors
- Vectors and scalars
- Vector addition/subtraction, scalar multiplication
- Dot product

### Matrices
- Important types of matrices
- Matrix transposition
- Matrix addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication
- Matrix multiplication

### Determinants
- Solving for a determinant
- Worked full example

### Inverse Matrices
- Deriving the inverse of a 2×2 matrix
- Inverting 2×2 and 3×3 matrices (minors, cofactor matrix, transpose)

### Matrix & Vector Properties
- Linear independence
- Matrix rank

### Systems of Equations as Matrices
- Solving systems via matrix inversion, worked example
- Overdetermined systems of equations
- Best-fit line via matrices (connects back to OLS from Lecture 4)

## Notes for the 2026 redesign

- Topic flow across the week runs: algebra/functions/limits → probability →
  differential calculus → integral/multivariate calculus → linear algebra,
  with OLS introduced twice (as a multivariate-calculus application in
  Lecture 4, and derived via matrices in Lecture 5).
- Candidate spots for interactive visualizations: set operations (Venn
  diagrams), function graphing, limits, the Monty Hall problem, distribution
  shapes (PMF/PDF/CDF), tangent/secant lines, optimization surfaces,
  gradients/Hessian, and matrix operations (esp. determinants and inverses).
